subject: arcadeCabinet

Category: Object.
Subject: 1980s arcade cabinet.
Style: synthwave.

spec.name: Neon Drive '84 Arcade Cabinet
spec.description: A full-size upright 1980s arcade cabinet with synthwave styling: an indigo-black carcass, magenta and cyan neon trim, sunset-and-grid side art, a glowing CRT showing a retro driving scene, and a backlit marquee.
spec.layout: Static prop, no joints. Real upright-cabinet proportions: about 0.66 m wide at the carcass, 0.95 m deep (z -0.48 to +0.47) and 1.82 m tall, standing on y = 0 and facing +Z. Seen from the side, the silhouette is one polygon in (z, y) pairs: (-0.48,0) (0.40,0) (0.40,0.84) (0.47,0.86) (0.47,0.96) (0.15,1.08) (0.074,1.58) (0.22,1.58) (0.22,1.82) (-0.40,1.82) (-0.48,1.25), back to the start. From the front (+Z) to the back it reads as follows. A flat coin-door front, 0.40 m forward, fills the lower body from y 0 to 0.84. Above it an overhanging control deck slopes up from its front lip (z 0.47, y 0.96) to the monitor's bottom edge (z 0.15, y 1.08). The CRT bezel leans back about 9 degrees, running from [0,1.08,0.15] to [0,1.58,0.074]. A deeper backlit marquee box sits on top, its front face at z 0.22. A tall, slightly tapered back tower with a rear service door carries the full height. The two side panels (x ±0.30 to ±0.33, 3 cm thick) are extruded from the silhouette polygon and span the whole height. Everything else sits between them at |x| <= 0.30, except the deck lip and T-molding, which may reach |x| 0.33. The side-art layer sits on the outer faces at |x| 0.33 to 0.345, inset 0.02 m from every edge of the polygon. SYNTHWAVE STYLE: the carcass is near-black indigo (cabinetBlack, shellPurple). Magenta and cyan neon tubes and T-molding run every edge. Glowing parts, made with the glow kit, are the screen scene, the marquee lettering and panel, the neon strips, the buttons' lit caps and the coin-door lights. Chunky, bold, blocky shapes; flat colours only; small parts for every detail (screws, vents, grille slots, labels). No ground, no props, no scenery.

parts.builds: The carcass. (1) Both side panels, each a 3 cm extrusion of the side-profile polygon (x ±0.30 to ±0.33) in shellPurple with cabinetBlack edge strips; a thin T-molding (trimMagenta, glowing) runs around the front and top edges, and chrome screw heads sit on the flanks. (2) Solid cores between the sides so no gaps show: a lower block (|x|<=0.30, y 0 to 0.84, z -0.48 to 0.40) and an upper rear block (y 0.84 to 1.58, z -0.48 to 0.06). The cores are panelNavy and cabinetBlack. (3) A recessed kick strip (rubber) at the base, y 0 to 0.10. (4) The coin-door front, z 0.40, y 0.14 to 0.80: a steel bezel and two coin slots with small backlit yellow/red entry lamps, two coin-return flaps, a chrome lock cylinder, and a neonCyan underline. A small speaker-grille slot row sits above the door and a cabinetBlack lower front panel carries a trimMagenta stripe. (5) The back tower: a rear service door with a recessed frame, vent slots, a hinge pair, a latch, a power-cord inlet and a tiny cord loop, all in cabinetBlack, steel and rubber. A cyan strip runs vertically at the rear corners.
parts.attaches: Side panels follow the full silhouette and host the sideArt layer on their outer faces at sideArtX. The lower block's top at lowerBodyTop is flush under the controlDeck. The upper rear block's front face at z 0.06 sits behind the monitor (monitorBottomEdge to monitorTopEdge). The tower top meets the marquee at cabinetTop.

parts.builds: The synthwave decal art on both outer flanks (build for s = +1 and -1; mirror it so the art faces outward on each side). Thin 8 mm layers at |x| 0.33 to 0.345, drawn in (z, y) on the silhouette polygon and kept 0.02 m inside its edges. Contents: a vertical dusk gradient made of stacked bands (shellPurple, mountainDark, screenSky2, sunPink); a big sun disc (sunYellow to sunOrange to sunPink) with horizontal slits cut by cabinetBlack stripes, centred near z -0.02, y 1.05; two layered jagged mountain ridges (mountainDark behind, mountainMid in front) on the horizon at y 0.85; a perspective grid on the lower body below it (gridPink and neonCyan lines converging toward the sun); a column of small white and cyan stars in the upper area; a neonCyan and trimMagenta double outline following the profile 0.02 m in; and a small bold chrome-and-white 'NEON DRIVE' badge strip on the lower flank. Use extrudes, thin boxes and slabs as the shapes. The art may glow lightly.
parts.attaches: Sits on the outer faces of the shell's side panels at sideArtX (x ±0.33 to ±0.345). Must not cross the profile polygon or the monitor and marquee openings.

parts.builds: The overhanging control deck in a z-by-y wedge between the lower body top and the monitor bottom, spanning |x| <= 0.30 with a trimMagenta lip up to |x| 0.33 at the front. A sloped top panel (panelNavy with a cabinetBlack inset plate) runs from deckFront [0,0.96,0.46] up to deckBack [0,1.08,0.15] (about a 21 degree tilt). A chrome and rubber front lip (z 0.47, y 0.86 to 0.96) has a neonCyan glowing edge strip. On the panel: one arcade joystick at x -0.14, z 0.33 (steel shaft, a rubber boot, a big round buttonRed ball top, a chrome mounting plate with four screws, a cabinetBlack square gate plate). A cluster of six chunky round buttons in two rows of three at x 0.04 to 0.26, z 0.27 to 0.37, in buttonRed, buttonBlue, buttonYellow, buttonGreen, buttonYellow and buttonRed. Each button has a dark ring base, a glowing cap and a small white highlight. 1P and 2P start buttons (small flat squares glowing neonCyan and trimMagenta) at x ±0.04, z 0.20. Painted panel details built as small parts: a neonPurple swoosh stripe, white 'P1' and 'START' label plates made from tiny bars or svg textures, a sunset-gradient stripe made of small bars, arrow marks around the joystick, and hex screw heads. Speaker slots (a row of dark slits) sit on the deck's left edge.
parts.attaches: The back edge is at monitorBottomEdge / deckBack [0,1.08,0.15], flush with the monitor bezel's bottom. The underside rests on lowerBodyTop at z up to 0.40, the overhang runs to deckLipFront, and the sides lie between the shell side panels (sideInnerX).

parts.builds: The tilted CRT monitor face between deckBack and marquee, built on the plane from monitorBottomEdge [0,1.08,0.15] to monitorTopEdge [0,1.58,0.074], with width |x| <= 0.30. A cabinetBlack bezel slab, with a darker screenBlack inner mask, a rounded-look bevel built from several thin boxes and a steel inner frame step. A trimMagenta thin line and a neonCyan thin line run along the bezel's bottom edge. The curved glass is a slightly domed, flat-shaded screenBlack slab, 0.50 wide by 0.38 tall along the slope, centred on screenCenter [0,1.33,0.112] and facing screenNormal. The glowing scene on the glass (glow kit, built as thin parts or textured planes seated 3 mm off the glass): a sky of stacked gradient bands (screenSky1, screenSky2, sunPink), a big striped sun (sunYellow, sunOrange, sunPink with black slits), two layered mountain ridges (mountainDark, mountainMid), a perspective grid floor (gridPink and neonCyan lines converging to a horizon vanishing point), a few palmDark palm silhouettes at the road edge, a simple blocky retro sports-car silhouette seen from behind with two red tail-light parts (buttonRed), and HUD text blocks: 'SCORE 001980' at top left, 'HI 099999' at top centre, 'CREDIT 01' at bottom, as white bar or svg-texture pieces. A faint white diagonal glass-reflection streak sits over one corner, and a few tiny 'screw cover' corner caps and a thin glass-edge highlight finish it. Small side vents and a degauss-style label plate on the bezel's lower edge are optional.
parts.attaches: The bottom edge meets the controlDeck's back edge at monitorBottomEdge. The top edge meets the marquee underside at marqueeBottom (y 1.58). Its sides meet the inner faces of the shell side panels at sideInnerX. Its back rests against the shell's upper rear block (z 0.06).

parts.builds: The topper from y 1.58 to 1.82 and the cabinet's top cap, |x| <= 0.30 inside the side panels (z -0.40 to 0.22). A cabinetBlack header box with a recessed, backlit title panel on its front face at marqueeFront [0,1.70,0.22], 0.56 wide by 0.20 tall: a glowing panel in panelNavy to screenSky2 gradient stripes, with a big blocky 'NEON DRIVE' wordmark (chunky letters built as small bars or a texture, in neonCyan with trimMagenta shadow offset, glowing), an '84' badge in sunYellow, a small striped sun and a mountain strip. A thin chrome frame surrounds the panel. Along the marquee edges run glowing neon tubes (trimMagenta on top, neonCyan on the bottom) as thin round rods with small end caps and clips. A top cap slab with a rear ridge, two small speaker pods or grille bars at the sides, and a row of tiny light dots (the 'chase' bulbs) in white and sunYellow along the top front edge. Also builds the roof: the top surface at cabinetTop [0,1.82,-0.09], with a few cooling vent slits and a trimMagenta stripe, plus two small screw heads.
parts.attaches: The bottom face sits on the monitor's top edge at marqueeBottom (y 1.58) and on the shell's tower top. The side faces sit between the shell side panels (sideInnerX). The front face at marqueeFront protrudes 0.15 beyond the monitor top (z 0.22 vs 0.074).

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching out a static arcade cabinet model with no joints, working out realistic dimensions for an upright cabinet body in a synthwave style.

Now I'm breaking it into parts: the cabinet body with side art panels and coin door, an angled control panel with joystick and buttons, a glowing CRT screen with a synthwave sunset/grid scene, and a backlit marquee topper with neon tubing. I'm planning each part to carry its own decorative details like gradients, stripes, and mountains for visual richness.

I'm now working out the precise silhouette coordinates for the cabinet's profile, starting with the kickbase depth and height at the base of the unit.

Then I'm figuring out the control deck's forward lip and angled rear mount points, followed by the monitor section's tilt — positioning the bezel plane so it leans back from a lower front edge to a higher rear top point.

I'm working through the side panel profile as a single extruded outline, plotting the (z,y) points that trace the cabinet's silhouette from base up through the control deck overhang and into the monitor hood, adjusting coordinates where the shape needs to avoid cutting into the screen housing.

Back panel tapers up to 1.82 at the top. I'm reorganizing the build into five parts, with a shell part handling both side panels, front lower panel, kick toe, back panel, rear vented door, power cord, top/base, and interior fill boxes.

For sideArt, I'm placing synthwave decorations (sunset bands, grid lines, mountains, sun disc, stars, neon edges) on a thin flank layer just outside the shell, constrained to stay within the silhouette polygon that both parts share as a spec. Then controlDeck covers the deck box, angled panel, joysticks, buttons, trackball, and label plates, while a monitor part still needs defining.

Now I'm working out the monitor section with its bezel, glowing tube screen showing a sunset scene, and tilted angle, followed by the marquee with its backlit title panel, blocky glowing letters, neon tubes, and speaker pods. I'm also pinning down cabinet dimensions—carcass width, side panel thickness, and how the control deck and marquee align within those bounds so the deck overhang stays inside the side panel profile.

With the normal computed, I'm now defining the marquee section sitting above the monitor: its depth and height range, the front title panel dimensions, and how it connects to the monitor bezel via a small lip gap. I'm also working out overall cabinet width and height including side art and trim.

Now I'm locking in the color palette, keeping it under 24 colors, with deep indigo blacks and purples for the cabinet shell, magenta and cyan neon accents for trim, and a warm sunset gradient of yellows, oranges, and pinks plus mountain and sky tones for the screen content.

That gives 24 colors total, good. Now I'm thinking through the box layout for the cabinet shell—whether to make the side panels span the full height or split them into a lower cabinet section and a rear upper column, since overlapping boxes between parts need to share faces cleanly for the builder.

I'm deciding to let the shell own the full-height side panels, back, rear door, coin door, kick, interior filler blocks, and T-molding as one rich carcass piece, with everything else built inside or in front of it. For the rear tower, I'm defining a solid core box behind the monitor area to house the monitor housing.

Then I'm working out how the monitor part builds just the slanted bezel and screen plane in front of the hidden core, figuring out the exact z-boundaries so the core's front face stays behind the tilted screen. I'm also carving out a separate zone for the control deck as its own angled box between the core and the front, rather than merging it into the core.

Now I'm defining the remaining coordinate boxes — upper core, deck, monitor, and marquee — making sure the marquee width lines up with the side panels at x ±0.30, and checking whether the shell or marquee owns the top cap. I'm also nudging the side panel profile points slightly so the monitor bezel sits a touch forward of the core at the bottom and top transition points.

Now I'm defining the monitor bezel and screen geometry on the sloped plane, calculating the screen center depth and sizing margins, then moving to the deck's front lip and panel surface positioning.

Working out the control deck's tilt angle and matching its upper edge to meet the monitor's bottom edge for a seamless profile, then starting to sketch the coin door's front panel.

Now I'm mapping the full side silhouette as a sequence of coordinate points, defining the kick strip at the base, the deck slope, the monitor bezel angle, and the back panel slope near the top, trying to keep the outline coherent going around the cabinet.

I'm planning the side art placement within that polygon shape—a sun disc, horizon bands, perspective grid, mountain silhouette, stars, and a neon outline tracing the profile—and budgeting part counts across shell, side art, control deck, monitor, and marquee to stay under the total limit. For the marquee I'm considering a blocky "NEON RUNNER" title rendered as a glowing texture.

Now I'm naming the game "NEON DRIVE '84" and detailing the marquee panel with a recessed front face and a glowing neon tube cap on top. For the monitor screen, I'm designing a synthwave scene—gradient sky, striped sun, grid floor, mountains, a car silhouette, and HUD text—built as a mix of small glowing parts and SVG textures, then moving to figure out the control deck layout and joystick positioning relative to the viewer's perspective.

Settling on joystick position and a button row layout, with start buttons placed near the back of the panel. Now I'll write the JSON output including mounts, a note on box overlaps, empty joints array, and a concise but sufficient layout description.

I'm sketching out a static side-profile silhouette for the body shape using a defined polygon of coordinates, planning to keep the geometry simple without articulated joints.

Working out the extrusion direction and layering offsets, stacking thin detail layers at slightly staggered x-positions so they sit just outside the panel surface without overlapping incorrectly.

I'm now worried about keeping these bands clipped to the actual polygon shape since it's concave—clipping against half-planes risks creating degenerate touching edges, so I'm considering clipping to simple rectangles instead to avoid self-intersecting geometry.

Defining simplified left/right boundary functions by y-range...

Still refining breakpoints...

Checking the back edge values against my left-side points confirms they match closely enough. Now I'm working out a band-building approach: sampling y-coordinates at endpoints and breakpoints from the right and left point lists, then constructing polygons by tracing up the right side and down the left, deduplicating close points to avoid self-intersection.

I'm planning the dusk gradient color bands from bottom to top—shellPurple near the ground, mountainDark above that, then sunPink near the horizon, followed by screenSky2 and mountainDark again higher up, with shellPurple returning at the very top for a layered sunset effect.

I'm also working out the sun's disc shape, building it from horizontal stripe segments clipped to a circular boundary, with colors shifting from yellow at the top through orange to pink near the horizon where it meets the ground.

Still writing slit stripe logic...

Now I'm working out the mountain ridgelines as jagged polygons layered above the sky but constrained within the valid z-range near the horizon, making sure the peaks near the deck stay low enough to fit the perspective limits at those heights.

Finishing up the mountain ridge points to keep the polygons simple and non-self-crossing, then moving on to the grid for the lower body, using horizontal lines spaced with perspective so they compress toward the horizon.

Now I'm working out the converging vertical lines for the grid, fanning from a vanishing point down to the bottom edge, and building each as a thin quad that tapers in width from bottom to top to fake perspective depth.

I'm alternating cyan and pink colors for the verticals and horizontals, adding a thick cyan horizon line, and planning to apply a glow kit with moderate strength to the neon elements since extruded parts support flat-color glow. Finally I'm tallying up the rough part count across bands, sun, mountains, grid lines, and stars to keep the scene budget in check.

Still positioning sweep rods...

Now thinking about stars: scattering small cube clusters in the upper sky region, constraining their z and y so they sit within the visible band between the mountain layers, mostly white/cyan with a few bigger plus-shaped ones for variety.

I'm also planning a chrome badge plate on the lower flank reading "NEON DRIVE" using a blocky pixel-font approach, sizing individual letter cells and spacing them to fit a plate roughly .27 wide by .05 tall.

Defining pixel-font letters...

I also need to figure out orientation: since I'm placing text on opposite faces of the model, I should mirror it appropriately so it reads correctly when viewed from each side, which means working out which direction is "right" relative to each face's outward normal.

I'll also set up a generic collector that groups geometries by color so I can merge them into fewer parts per side, reusing it for stars, badge letters, and grid lines all built in local model-space coordinates.

Still defining coordinate arrays...

Still assembling grid geometry...

For stars I'm randomizing a small cluster near the top with varied sizes and colors, mirroring positions across both sides so they stay symmetric. Then I'm setting up a badge plate with a chrome border, thin magenta underline accent, and white lettering on a navy background.

Working out layer depths now, limiting the stacking offset so the plate, navy inset, and raised letters stay within bounds -- plate at one depth, navy panel slightly forward, letters on top, all white since the chrome-and-white look doesn't need extra color.

I'm figuring out the letter spacing and text positioning formula: each character cell gets a fixed pitch, and depending on which side the text reads from, I derive a position formula that starts from a center point and offsets by cumulative cell width times direction sign, so the text reads correctly whether approached from either side.

For the row positions, I'm computing vertical centers similarly, then merging consecutive filled cells into single rectangles sized by run length so adjacent segments render as one continuous bar rather than separate blocks. I'll just destructure the provided context object as given and write the function to return nothing, relying on the module's glow import for visuals.
